excerpt: November 2026 edition How AI like ChatGPT works, updated every month Most of us use AI tools every day without knowing what happens between typing a question and getting an answer. This guide explains it from the ground up, in plain language, with diagrams you can try. Here for security? Start with prompt injection (14 min, no earlier chapters needed). Your text, as tokens Through the layers Next-token probabilities Part 1: Language models How a language model turns text into numbers, predicts the next word and learns from data, and where that breaks down. Each chapter has a demo to try and three questions at the end. New to this? Start with chapter 1; otherwise jump around. What an LLM is, in five minutes The whole picture in five minutes: what these systems are, how they were built and what they are not. Text becomes tokens, tokens become numbers Models never see letters or words. They see numbered pieces of text, and then points on a map of meaning. Attention: how words borrow meaning How each word looks back at the earlier words and pulls in what it needs. This is the core mechanism of the transformer. Inside the stack Each layer gathers context from other words and then processes it, and a model repeats that dozens of times. Also: the trick that lets giant models run cheaply. Generating text, one token at a time Each word is a weighted dice roll. That explains why answers differ every time, what "temperature" does and why thinking takes time. Training: from autocomplete to assistant to agent A model goes through five training stages, and each one changes what it does. Knowing them explains a lot of everyday behaviour. Is it really just predicting the next word? Technically, it is. Training, the model's internal representations and the tool loop explain why a coding agent can still do far more than autocomplete.
